newsitem.title: USA: Xerox sees price pressure from Kodak deal.
newsitem.headline: Xerox sees price pressure from Kodak deal.

text.p: Xerox Corp expects pricing pressure in the wake of the deal for Danka Business Systems Plc to buy Eastman Kodak Co's office copier business for $684 million.

"Suffice to say that Danka has been aggressive, and will continue to be aggressive," said Gil Hatch, vice president and general manager of the Xerox department copier business unit. "Danka has built its copier business through acquisitions, and has pretty good distribution capacity."
Hatch declined to say what pricing changes Xerox would make in the wake of the Kodak deal. "They're on our turf now and are going to have to chase us to win this business," he said.

Hatch said he expects that, while Kodak struggled to make money in the copier business, it succeeded in building strong customer relationships. "The issue for (Danka) now is to sell to the customer base," and keep the relationships strong, he said.
Hatch said he doesn't expect Xerox "to make any significant changes" in light of the deal.

Hatch declined to discuss unit revenues, except to say that it was the largest Xerox unit. A Xerox spokesman said total revenues should reach about $17 billion this year, up from $16.6 billion in 1995.
Xerox shares fell 1/2 to 57-3/8. Danka ADRs jumped five to 34-7/8, while Kodak fell 1/2 to 71-3/4.
